key_facts: Third quarter sales were $122.4 million, up 8% compared to the third quarter of 2020 and down 6% sequentially from the second quarter.
Customer demand remains robust, while supply challenges persist, especially for transportation products.
Third quarter gross margin was 37.3%, up 490 basis points from 32.4% in the third quarter of 2020 and up 50 basis points sequentially from the second quarter of 2021.
Third quarter EBITDA margin was 21.7%, up 270 basis points from 19% in the third quarter of 2020.
Third quarter adjusted earnings per share were $0.46, up 35% from $0.34 in the third quarter of 2020.
Operating cash flow for the third quarter was $21 million, down from $26 million in the third quarter of 2020.
New business awards for the third quarter were $179 million, up from $127 million in the same period last year.
Sales to transportation customers declined by 5% compared to the third quarter of 2020 and 13% sequentially.
Sales to other end markets increased 24% year-over-year and 3% sequentially.
The non-transportation related revenue accounted for nearly 50% of total revenue in the third quarter.
The semiconductor shortage is expected to reduce vehicle builds by nine million to 10 million units this year.
The U.S. light vehicle transportation market SAAR dropped closer to $12 million in September, with an expected range of 13 to 13.5 million units for the year.
On-hand days supply are now closer to 20 days, the lowest in recent history, down over 60% from the five-year average of 55 days.
The third quarter reported a loss of $1.97 per share, while adjusted earnings were $0.46 per diluted share compared to $0.34 per diluted share in the same period last year.
A noncash charge of $106 million before tax was recorded as part of the U.S. pension plan termination process.
The third quarter tax rate was 28.9%, with an anticipated 2021 tax rate range of 19% to 21% excluding the pension settlement and other discrete items.
The company's cash balance was $129 million as of September 30, 2021, up from $92 million on December 31, 2020.
Long-term debt balance was $50 million at the end of the third quarter, down from $55 million on December 31, 2020.
The debt to capitalization ratio was 9.9% at the end of the third quarter, compared to 11.4% at the end of 2020.
The company is near the end of its SAP system rollout, with most sites now running on SAP and completion expected in early 2022.
The company is committed to further diversifying its business, with a focus on non-transportation related revenue growth.
The company repurchased approximately 148,000 shares for slightly less than $5 million as part of its stock buyback program.
The company's M&A strategy focuses on enhancing technology and product capabilities, geographic reach, and EV offerings, targeting acquisitions up to $50 million in sales.
The company expects supply chain challenges to persist for the rest of the year and into 2022, impacting both material availability and costs.
The company's restructuring program achieved $0.03 in earnings per share savings in the third quarter, with targeted annualized savings of $0.22 to $0.26 of earnings per share by the end of 2022.
The company's balance sheet is strong, bolstered by solid cash flow generation, providing a competitive advantage for its diversification strategy.
The company's guidance for full year 2021 was updated to sales in the range of $495 million to $505 million and adjusted earnings in the range of $1.85 to $1.95 per share.

The company's focus on diversification includes expanding into industrial, medical, aerospace, and defense markets, with notable growth in temperature sensing, RF filters, and transducer applications.
The company added two new industrial customers in the third quarter, one for an RF filter application and the other for a temperature-controlled crystal component applied in a GPS application.
The company's non-transportation end market performed strongly, with sales increasing 24% year-over-year and 3% sequentially.
The company's industrial sales advanced due to robust demand for temperature products in pool and spa, HVAC, and other applications.
The company's medical end market showed continued growth, with wins in drug delivery, ultrasound, and temperature sensing applications.
The company's defense market saw growth with undersea sonar and RF filter programs, and it is testing samples for underwater unmanned vehicle applications.
The company's transportation business is expected to continue facing supply challenges, but it performed better than the outlook provided in the last quarterly update.
The company's long-term strategy includes diversifying its end market profile, expanding technologies, products, customers, and geographic reach.
The company's focus on extending into hot side applications is gaining momentum, with shipments to a new customer expected later in the year.
The company's restructuring activities are on track to achieve targeted annualized savings of $0.22 to $0.26 of earnings per share by the end of 2022.
The company's global team continues to demonstrate strong execution and commitment to operational excellence and long-term goals.
The company launched CTS Cares, a new platform for community engagement and charitable giving, as part of its efforts to bolster engagement in its communities.
The company's 125th anniversary is being celebrated with a focus on giving back to communities through the CTS Cares program.
